heroes.hook: A single figure turns thought itself into sculpture.
heroes.summary_en: A serene gilt-bronze bodhisattva whose crossed leg, lowered gaze, and slight smile have become an emblem of Korean Buddhist art.
heroes.summary_ko: 반가의 자세, 내려앉은 시선, 미소가 한국 불교조각의 상징이 된 금동 보살상입니다.
heroes.credit: Photo by Slices of Light via Wikimedia Commons; identity confirmed by National Museum of Korea
heroes.verification_note: Exact National Treasure No. 83 object; Commons licensing retained with attribution.

heroes.name_en: Celadon Prunus Vase with Inlaid Cloud and Crane Design
heroes.hook: A vase where cranes drift through jade-green air.
heroes.summary_en: The iconic Goryeo celadon maebyeong, celebrated for its cloud-and-crane inlay and taut, elegant silhouette.
heroes.summary_ko: 운학문 상감과 팽팽한 실루엣으로 고려청자의 정수를 보여주는 매병입니다.
heroes.needs_verification: Image withheld: current local reusable image is a similar Goryeo cloud-and-crane maebyeong, not confirmed as Kansong National Treasure No. 68.
heroes.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art public-domain image; retained only as hidden reference until exact NT68 source is secured
heroes.verification_note: Do not display a photo until an exact reusable Kansong NT68 image is confirmed.

heroes.hook: The most radical gesture here is emptiness.
heroes.summary_en: A full, white porcelain form whose slight asymmetry turns restraint into presence.
heroes.summary_ko: 순백의 둥근 형태와 미세한 비대칭이 조선 미감의 절제를 보여주는 달항아리입니다.
heroes.credit: Cultural Heritage Administration / Korea Heritage Service via Wikimedia Commons
heroes.verification_note: Exact National Treasure No. 310 image; local filename corrected from nt262 to nt310.

heroes.designation: National Treasure No. 70 / UNESCO Memory of the World
heroes.hook: A writing system appears with its own source code.
heroes.summary_en: The book that explains why Hangul was invented and how its letters work.
heroes.summary_ko: 한글이 왜 만들어졌고 어떻게 작동하는지 설명하는 문자 창제의 원본 기록입니다.
heroes.needs_verification: Image withheld: reusable Commons image is documented as a reprint/facsimile, not confirmed as the exact Kansong Haerye manuscript object.
heroes.credit: Kyujanggak/SNU reprint scan via Wikimedia Commons; hidden until exact original-manuscript status is resolved
heroes.verification_note: Do not display unless the page is relabeled as a facsimile/reprint or an exact original source is confirmed.

heroes.hook: A crown that looks less worn than grown.
heroes.summary_en: A Silla gold crown whose tree-like uprights and jade pendants turn royal power into ritual landscape.
heroes.summary_ko: 나뭇가지 모양 입식과 곡옥 장식이 신라 왕권과 제의를 압축한 금관입니다.
heroes.credit: Korea Heritage Service via Wikimedia Commons
heroes.verification_note: Exact National Treasure No. 87 image; local file refreshed from Commons original.

heroes.name_en: Great Gilt-bronze Incense Burner of Baekje
heroes.hook: A whole mountain smokes inside a ritual vessel.
heroes.summary_en: A phoenix, mountain lid, lotus body, and dragon base combine into Baekje’s most theatrical bronze object.
heroes.summary_ko: 봉황, 산악형 뚜껑, 연꽃 몸체, 용 받침이 한 몸을 이룬 백제 공예의 절정입니다.
heroes.credit: Rheo1905 via Wikimedia Commons; identity confirmed by Buyeo National Museum
heroes.verification_note: Exact National Treasure No. 287 object; local JPEG byte-matches Commons upload.

heroes.hook: A sculpture you are meant to hear.
heroes.summary_en: A monumental Unified Silla bell whose reliefs, inscription, and resonance made it a model for Korean Buddhist bells.
heroes.summary_ko: 부조와 명문, 울림으로 한국 범종의 기준이 된 통일신라의 거대한 청동 종입니다.
heroes.credit: Wikimedia Commons CC0 image; identity confirmed by Gyeongju National Museum
heroes.verification_note: Exact National Treasure No. 29 object; placeholder SVG replaced by local JPEG.

heroes.name_en: Printing Woodblocks of the Tripiṭaka Koreana
heroes.hook: A library carved so carefully it became architecture.
heroes.summary_en: More than 80,000 Buddhist printing blocks, carved in Goryeo as a monumental act of preservation.
heroes.summary_ko: 고려가 새긴 8만여 장의 불교 경전 목판으로, 지식 보존의 거대한 시스템입니다.
heroes.credit: Wikimedia Commons CC0 image of Tripitaka Koreana at Haeinsa
heroes.verification_note: Exact Haeinsa Tripitaka Koreana woodblocks image; wrong copy-block fallback removed.

heroes.hook: The new dynasty wrote its sky in stone.
heroes.summary_en: A Joseon star chart that maps constellations, seasons, and royal legitimacy onto a dark slab.
heroes.summary_ko: 별자리와 계절, 왕조의 정당성을 검은 돌 위에 새긴 조선의 천문도입니다.
heroes.credit: National Palace Museum of Korea / KOGL Type 1
heroes.verification_note: Exact National Treasure No. 228 image; placeholder SVG replaced by official local JPEG.

heroes.name_en: Album of Genre Paintings by Kim Hong-do (Danwon)
heroes.hook: After kings and Buddhas, ordinary people take the stage.
heroes.summary_en: Kim Hong-do’s genre album brings labor, play, humor, and movement into the hero sequence.
heroes.summary_ko: 김홍도의 풍속도첩은 노동과 놀이, 유머와 움직임을 히어로 목록 안으로 끌어옵니다.
heroes.credit: Wikimedia Commons public-domain reproduction; identity confirmed by National Museum of Korea
heroes.verification_note: Exact Ssireum leaf from Kim Hong-do genre album.
